messages:
Maya: Dropped an initial RFC draft for "Adaptive Kernel Routing + KV Cache Policy". Link: https://rwd/drive/rfc/adaptive-kernel-2026
Liam: Quick q — is the plan a global toggle or per-model policy?
Maya: Per-model/per-deployment rules. Product wants a Console "Adaptive Serving" switch that applies a recommended profile by default.
Sofia: Product needs concrete launch gates. Can we list acceptance criteria?
Rachel: From ops: p99 latency shouldn't exceed current baseline by more than 5ms on our standard perf curves; overall token spend reduced by >=8% on mixed workloads; zero regressions on top-3 customer flows.
Liam: Also require safe rollback: ability to force previous kernel set via env var and immediate revert in canary.
Maya: Agreed. Add end-to-end perfbench scenarios for seq_len 128/512/2048 and batch sizes 1/4/16, plus quantized (4-bit) models.
Sofia: Edge cases to enumerate: very high prefix diversity (cache thrash), cold-KV warmup latencies, multi-tenant eviction fairness.
deploy-bot: Canary pipeline created: canary/adaptive-kernel -> steps 1% -> 10% -> 50% (manual approvals)
Liam: Kernel heuristic inputs: model class (decoder vs encoder-decoder), observed KV hit-rate, seq_len histograms, and hardware family (A100/H100).
Sofia: For attention: enable fused/flash-style kernels up to seq_len 1024, use tiled/fallback attn beyond that. Note `use_flash` has memory-safety bounds when session tokens > 1.5M.
Maya: Will add validation tests for attention fallback and metrics to track fallback ratio per seq_len bucket.
Rachel: Launch checklist: RFC approvals (eng-runtime + eng-ml), perfbench green, Console toggle implemented, canary + SLA monitoring, docs + runbook, deprecation notes for legacy kernels.
Liam: Draft per-model config snippet:

```
{
  "model": "gpt-xxl-8k",
  "adaptive_serving": true,
  "kernel_policy": {
    "preferred": ["flash-fused","flash-quant"],
    "fallback": ["tiled-attn"],
    "seq_thresholds": {"flash-fused": 1024}
  },
  "kv_cache": {"policy": "LRU", "per_tenant_limit": 64, "eviction_grace_ms": 500}
}
```

Maya: Test `per_tenant_limit` under heavy-sharding and multi-tenant load.
Sofia: KV cache targets: +10% hit rate on warm traces, eviction-induced latency <20ms at p95.
Liam: Testing plan: synthetic traces for worst-case prefix diversity, replays of top customer workloads, randomized config fuzzing.
Rachel: Telemetry must tag requests with kernel_variant, kv_hit, kv_evicted, seq_len_bucket, model_version. Also emit estimated_token_cost_delta per request.
Maya: Rollout policy: internal/staging -> 1% low-SLA customers -> 10% -> full over two weeks if thresholds pass. Halt if p99 latency increases >8% or error-rate spikes.
Sofia: Add Console alert for cohort cost increases >5%.
Maya: Owners: Maya (RFC author & product), Liam (kernel heuristics + runtime), Sofia (attention & KV tests), Rachel (rollout, metrics, docs).
Rachel: Product blurb: "Adaptive kernel routing + KV cache policies to lower token cost and stabilize latency for mixed workloads — canary H2 2026."
Maya: I'll push the RFC update and request reviews from eng-ml and eng-sre. Thanks all :rocket:
